title: Light–Dark Circadian Entrainment
mission: Synchronise the central circadian clock with the external light–dark cycle through retinal light signals.

findings.statement: In a retrospective analysis of 116 healthy adults aged 18–30, room light before bedtime suppressed melatonin and shortened its duration by about 90 minutes relative to dim light.
Human light exposures can advance or delay circadian phase, depending on their timing.
Intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells provide a biological route for retinal light signals; melanopsin photosensitivity depends on a vitamin A-based chromophore.

sop.input: Timed bright-light exposure
Dim-light comparison before bedtime
Printed-book comparison with evening eReader use

title: Feeding-Time Circadian Synchronisation
mission: Coordinate peripheral metabolic clock timing through feeding cues.

findings.statement: In ten healthy men, a five-hour meal delay shifted glucose rhythm timing by 5.69 ± 1.29 hours and adipose PER2 by 0.97 ± 0.29 hours, without significant changes in measured melatonin or cortisol timing.
Animal feeding manipulations shift peripheral clock rhythms while central-clock phase remains linked to the light cycle.

sop.input: Defined meal-timing schedule

title: NAPE → NAE Biosynthesis Capacity
mission: Enable NAPE-to-NAE biosynthesis so endocannabinoidome signalling lipids remain available for stress and motivation regulation.

findings.statement: N-arachidonoyl phosphatidylethanolamine and its biosynthetic pathway were identified in brain preparations.
The membrane substrate enters a binuclear zinc active centre; bile acids influence enzyme organisation and activity.
PE-containing meals did not improve the tested satiety or energy-intake endpoints.

inputs.role: NAPE supplies the acyl-ethanolamine moiety released during NAE formation.
Intracellular phosphatidylethanolamine supplies the backbone used to form N-acyl phosphatidylethanolamine.
Two active-site zinc ions support human NAPE-PLD hydrolysis.

title: Omega-3-Derived Endocannabinoidome Signalling
mission: Sustain omega-3-derived ethanolamide production so endocannabinoidome neuromodulation stays supplied from dietary fat status.

findings.statement: Both exposures supplied N-docosahexaenoyl-PE and synaptamide; equimolar free DHA generated more synaptamide.
DHA-enriched oil increased its corresponding plasma ethanolamide. EPA-containing arms had higher plasma EPEA than DHA alone; combined exposure also changed DHEA.

inputs.role: DHA supplies the acyl chain used to form N-docosahexaenoyl-PE and synaptamide.
EPA supply supports formation of its corresponding ethanolamide, EPEA.

title: FAAH-Mediated Endocannabinoid Preservation
mission: Preserve endocannabinoid signalling duration by limiting FAAH-mediated degradation of anandamide and related NAEs.

findings.statement: FAAH inhibition prolonged the rapid CB1-sensitive dopamine response; a later component differed pharmacologically.
Genistein and daidzein altered anandamide uptake under the tested laboratory conditions.

inputs.role: Anandamide is a signalling lipid hydrolysed by FAAH; inhibition can prolong its effects.

title: Endocannabinoid–Dopamine Neuromodulation
mission: Shape dopaminergic reward and motivation pathways through endocannabinoid neuromodulatory interaction.

findings.statement: CB1 disruption reduced cue responses; augmenting 2-AG, rather than anandamide, enhanced the tested cue-linked response.
FAAH inhibition prolonged the rapid CB1-sensitive dopamine response; a later component differed pharmacologically.

inputs.role: Endogenous 2-AG signalling contributes to VTA CB1-dependent reward-cue dopamine modulation.

title: Endocannabinoid Stress-Buffering Capacity
mission: Sustain endocannabinoid-mediated stress buffering so HPA-axis and neuroinflammatory reactivity stay proportionate.

findings.statement: Restraint increased FAAH and reduced AEA; basolateral-amygdala FAAH inhibition attenuated corticosterone through a CB1-dependent route.
Moderate exercise increased circulating AEA; the full-sample threat response was lower at reinstatement.

title: Oestrogen Signalling Stability
mission: Maintain stable oestrogen-linked signalling so dopamine tone and emotional regulation remain steady across hormonal fluctuation.

findings.statement: Estradiol-related cognitive responses varied with dopamine-related baseline context.
Wheat bran reduced measured estrogens; oat and corn bran did not show the same result.

title: Estrobolome Regulation
mission: Shape systemic oestrogen exposure through microbiome-mediated regulation of oestrogen metabolism and recycling.

findings.statement: A subset of enzymes cleaved estrogen glucuronides; selective inhibition reduced ex-vivo reactivation.
Wheat bran reduced measured estrogens; oat and corn bran did not show the same result.

inputs.role: Specific microbial beta-glucuronidases release free estrogens from conjugated substrates.

title: Progesterone-Supportive Microbial Metabolism
mission: Sustain microbial contributions to progesterone-related hormonal stability through gut ecosystem function.

findings.statement: Hydrogen supported conversion of 3alpha,5alpha-THDOC into tetrahydroprogesterone products; human stool observations complemented the experiments.

inputs.role: This host-derived steroid supplies the substrate for the studied microbial progestin conversion.
Hydrogen supports the experimentally demonstrated microbial steroid conversion.

title: Metabolic-Reproductive Hormone Integration
mission: Enable coordinated integration of insulin and metabolic signalling with reproductive hormone balance.

findings.statement: Insulin stimulated testosterone production through its receptor and an inositolglycan-sensitive signalling route.
Completers showed better oral-test insulin sensitivity and menstrual cyclicity with low GI; reproductive hormone superiority was not established.

sop.input: Low-GI dietary pattern in PCOS

title: Testosterone Signalling Stability
mission: Maintain androgen receptor signalling so motivation, stamina, and goal-directed effort remain well supported.

findings.statement: Serum testosterone fell during restriction and rose during repletion in the small deficient groups.
Daytime testosterone was approximately 10–15% lower after restricted sleep; reported vigour also fell.

inputs.role: Adequate zinc supply supports testosterone availability; restriction and repletion studies identify a conditional upstream contribution to androgen ligand supply.

title: Androgen-Microbiome Regulation
mission: Shape systemic androgen exposure through microbiome-mediated androgen metabolism and recycling.

findings.statement: Microbiota enabled distal intestinal androgen deconjugation; local free DHT was high.
Hormone exposures changed microbial community and metabolic measurements.

inputs.role: Microbial metabolism releases free androgens from conjugated substrates within intestinal contents.

title: Amino-Acid Availability & Prioritisation
mission: Ensure meal-level protein supply delivers the amino-acid foundation neurotransmitter pathways depend on.

findings.statement: Dietary protein supplies phenylalanine to the human circulation, with delivery kinetics varying by the tested protein source, dose and meal context. The pooled age association is context-dependent, not proof that ageing uniformly impairs absorption or that greater availability increases brain neurotransmitters.

Varied adult diets can provide digestible indispensable amino acids without requiring every meal to supply the full set. This nutritional-adequacy proposition does not establish an optimal neurotransmitter dose or demonstrate that all plant and animal foods have identical postprandial responses.

Phenylalanine-4-hydroxylase (PAH) converts L-phenylalanine to L-tyrosine. This endogenous route contributes to tyrosine supply but does not make tyrosine absent from foods or establish an independent requirement for extra dietary tyrosine.

Tyrosine and tryptophan supply the precursor pathways for catecholamines and serotonin, respectively. Their biochemical identity does not demonstrate that additional meal protein improves brain transmitter synthesis, attention, mood or reward.

In a randomised crossover study of ten older men, 135 g minced beef produced greater six-hour dietary phenylalanine appearance than the same quantity of steak. Total plasma essential-amino-acid concentrations and muscle protein synthesis did not differ detectably between preparations.

In a randomised crossover of nine healthy young adults, the tested high-moisture-extruded mycoprotein/pea blend delayed selected early plasma amino-acid responses relative to the dry blend. Total five-hour grouped amino-acid availability was not significantly different; the study does not establish poorer overall nutrition for all meat alternatives.

inputs.role: Coverage of the indispensable amino-acid set, including phenylalanine, that sets the circulating pool neurotransmitter pathways can draw on. Meals contribute measurable amino-acid composition; this is not a requirement that each meal provide complete coverage

Catecholamine precursor in the circulating pool this PM prioritises. Tyrosine is normally formed from indispensable phenylalanine and can become conditionally indispensable when phenylalanine availability is limited
Indispensable serotonergic precursor this PM prioritises in the circulating precursor pool

title: LAT1 Competitive Transport Modulation
mission: Influence competition for transport across the blood–brain barrier so neurotransmitter precursors can reach the brain after meals.

findings.statement: Large neutral amino acids share competitive transport through LAT1 (SLC7A5) with the SLC3A2 heavy chain; plasma composition helps shape substrate availability but is not a direct measurement of net brain uptake.

In the studied healthy adults, meal composition and tested protein sources can alter plasma tryptophan relative to competing large neutral amino acids; the direction and tyrosine response depend on the exposure and sampling context, without establishing increased human brain transport or neurotransmitter synthesis.

The ordinary-meal studies assessed here measured plasma amino-acid ratios, not brain transport or ADHD outcomes; findings from enriched-protein attention studies do not establish ordinary-meal efficacy.
Plasma large-neutral-amino-acid ratio change after a meal is not equivalent to measured brain transport, monoamine synthesis or a Phenome outcome.

inputs.role: Large-neutral amino acid that competes for LAT1-mediated brain entry
Large-neutral amino acid that competes for LAT1-mediated brain entry
Regulates plasma tryptophan- and tyrosine-to-LNAA ratios at LAT1 after a meal

title: Dopaminergic Signalling Regulation
mission: Maintain appropriately regulated dopamine synthesis, storage, release, receptor signalling, reuptake and metabolism across changing functional demand.

findings.statement: Neuronal dopamine synthesis depends on separable tyrosine-hydroxylase and aromatic L-amino-acid-decarboxylase reactions with iron, tetrahydrobiopterin and pyridoxal-5′-phosphate requirements; cofactor requirement is not evidence of intake responsiveness.
Dopaminergic modulation of working memory and cognitive control follows baseline-, region- and process-dependent nonlinear relationships rather than a uniformly beneficial direction.
Striatal dopamine synthesis capacity and controlled dopaminergic manipulation influence cognitive-effort choice by altering benefit-versus-cost weighting.
Dopamine, including D2-receptor signalling, contributes to cognitive flexibility and set shifting in a task- and baseline-dependent manner.
Healthy aging is associated with declines in dopamine receptor and transporter availability but not a significant pooled decline in dopamine synthesis capacity.
ADHD-related dopamine findings are heterogeneous across synthesis, release, receptors and transporter measures and do not establish a uniform global dopamine deficit.
Open-label L-tyrosine supplementation did not produce a sustained ADHD benefit and did not demonstrate modification of brain dopamine biology.
Ascorbic-acid pairing and validated phytate degradation can increase meal-level non-haem iron absorption in matrix-dependent human studies, but no direct dopamine effect has been demonstrated.
Acute voluntary cardiovascular exercise can elicit dorsal-striatal dopamine release in healthy adults, with the measured release associated with faster reaction time.
One night of total sleep deprivation reduces ventral-striatal D2/D3 receptor availability in healthy adults and is associated with reduced alertness.
Short-term selective fat restriction and very-low-calorie dieting can alter regional D2/D3 receptor binding potential in adults with obesity under controlled research conditions.
Remethylation can replenish methionine for SAM synthesis; human COMT uses SAM to methylate dopamine.
The reviewed LNAA pool supplies tyrosine upstream of dopamine synthesis.
Phenylalanine can replenish circulating tyrosine upstream of dopamine synthesis; precursor conversion is not evidence that additional intake increases neuronal output.

inputs.role: Cofactor required by tyrosine hydroxylase during catecholamine synthesis
Cofactor for aromatic L-amino-acid decarboxylase conversion of L-DOPA to dopamine
Dietary route to PLP, the active cofactor for aromatic L-amino-acid decarboxylase. This is not an independent dopamine-synthesis cofactor
Tyrosine is the substrate for conversion to L-DOPA in dopamine synthesis.
Endogenous cofactor required by tyrosine hydroxylase during conversion of tyrosine to L-DOPA

Folate supplies the methyl group through [BRS2 PM1 — Folate/B12 remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm1-folate-b12-dependent-homocysteine-remethylation), replenishing methionine used by [BRS2 PM3 — MAT/SAM synthesis](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm3-same-synthesis). SAM is the methyl donor used by COMT during dopamine metabolism.

Betaine donates methyl groups through [BRS2 PM2 — BHMT remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation), predominantly in liver and kidney, replenishing methionine upstream of [BRS2 PM3 — SAM synthesis](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm3-same-synthesis). SAM is used by COMT during dopamine metabolism.

Choline can be oxidised to betaine for [BRS2 PM2 — BHMT remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation), predominantly in liver and kidney, replenishing methionine upstream of [BRS2 PM3 — SAM synthesis](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm3-same-synthesis). SAM is used by COMT during dopamine metabolism.

Phenylalanine is hydroxylated to tyrosine in peripheral tissues, replenishing the circulating tyrosine available to [LAT1 transport](/docs/biological-targets/brs1/fm1/brs1-fm1-pm2-lat1-competitive-transport-modulation) upstream of dopamine synthesis.

title: Noradrenergic Signalling
mission: Support noradrenergic alertness and executive control so attention and arousal stay appropriately engaged.

findings.statement: Noradrenaline modulates arousal, vigilance and executive-control processes by changing the gain of multiple central-nervous-system cell types rather than acting as a single directional attention chemical.

Noradrenaline formation depends on the shared tyrosine-to-dopamine catecholamine sequence, including iron- and PLP-dependent enzyme steps; cofactor or substrate necessity is not evidence of intake-responsive human brain noradrenaline.

Conversion of dopamine to noradrenaline by dopamine β-hydroxylase requires enzyme-bound copper and ascorbate as the electron donor; those biochemical requirements are not evidence of intake-responsive human brain noradrenaline or a functional benefit.

Repository evidence supports a translational relationship from noradrenergic signalling to Focus / Attention Stability without establishing dietary modification of noradrenaline or an ADHD treatment effect.
LAT1-related precursor presentation, heterogeneous dopamine-process measures and insulin–dopamine reward reviews are not interchangeable with noradrenergic signalling.
Prefrontal catecholamine regulation includes receptor-dependent actions and shared regional clearance, rather than separate linear precursor-to-transmitter pathways.
In a monkey vigilance task, locus-coeruleus neurons showed target-linked phasic activity that varied with performance.
Remethylation can replenish methionine for SAM synthesis; human COMT uses SAM to methylate noradrenaline.
The reviewed LNAA pool supplies tyrosine upstream of noradrenaline synthesis.
Phenylalanine can replenish circulating tyrosine upstream of noradrenaline synthesis; precursor conversion is not evidence that additional intake increases neuronal output.

Required metal cofactor of dopamine β-hydroxylase in the conversion of dopamine to noradrenaline
Electron donor that keeps the copper sites of dopamine β-hydroxylase reduced so dopamine can be hydroxylated to noradrenaline

SAM is the methyl donor used by COMT during noradrenaline metabolism.

Betaine donates methyl groups through [BRS2 PM2 — BHMT remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation), predominantly in liver and kidney, replenishing methionine upstream of [BRS2 PM3 — SAM synthesis](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm3-same-synthesis). SAM is used by COMT during noradrenaline metabolism.

Choline can be oxidised to betaine for [BRS2 PM2 — BHMT remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation), predominantly in liver and kidney, replenishing methionine upstream of [BRS2 PM3 — SAM synthesis](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm3-same-synthesis). SAM is used by COMT during noradrenaline metabolism.

title: Serotonergic Signalling Regulation
mission: Support serotonergic signalling so mood stability, inhibition, and behavioural regulation remain well grounded.

findings.statement: Serotonin modulates emotional processing, impulse control and behavioural regulation rather than acting as a single directional mood chemical.

Serotonin formation depends on tryptophan-hydroxylase conversion of tryptophan to 5-hydroxytryptophan, requiring iron and BH4, followed by PLP-dependent decarboxylation; cofactor or substrate necessity is not evidence of intake-responsive human brain serotonin.

Serotonergic signalling includes vesicular handling, receptor-mediated actions, transporter-mediated reuptake and enzymatic metabolism; those stages are not interchangeable with precursor supply and are not evidence of dietary control.

Repository and bounded-review evidence supports a translational relationship from serotonergic signalling to Emotional Regulation without establishing dietary modification of serotonin or an ADHD treatment effect.
LAT1-related precursor presentation is not interchangeable with serotonergic signalling.

inputs.role: Substrate for tryptophan hydroxylase conversion to 5-hydroxytryptophan, the immediate precursor of serotonin
Cofactor for aromatic L-amino-acid decarboxylase conversion of 5-hydroxytryptophan to serotonin
Provides dietary B6 vitamers that are converted to PLP
Required metal cofactor of tryptophan hydroxylase during conversion of tryptophan to 5-hydroxytryptophan
Endogenous cofactor required by tryptophan hydroxylase during conversion of tryptophan to 5-hydroxytryptophan

title: Acetylcholine Synthesis Support
mission: Maintain the capacity to form acetylcholine so cholinergic signalling for attention, working memory, and learning stays supplied.

findings.statement: Sodium-coupled high-affinity choline uptake through CHT/SLC5A7 is required to recover choline into cholinergic nerve terminals and commonly limits acetylcholine production under physiological demand.
Acetylcholine is formed from choline and acetyl-CoA by choline acetyltransferase; biochemical necessity is not intake-responsive human brain acetylcholine.
Dietary phosphatidylcholine is digested and remodelled into circulating phosphatidylcholine and free choline, establishing a dietary provision route to the direct choline substrate.
Pantothenate supports acetylcholine-synthesis capacity through coenzyme A and acetyl-CoA formation, and severe chronic pantothenate depletion can reduce brain acetylcholine synthesis in rats.

Inadequate folate-dependent or B12-dependent methionine-cycle capacity can disturb brain choline metabolism and lower acetylcholine availability, creating a supported shared-resource constraint on acetylcholine-synthesis capacity.
Cytosolic acetyl-CoA for acetylcholine synthesis is supplied through compartmented neuronal metabolism, and its availability can regulate synthesis independently of choline transport.
Human ADHD-related muscarinic-binding and choline-status evidence is translationally relevant to attention; it is not a demonstration that changing choline intake treats ADHD.

inputs.role: Direct substrate combined with acetyl-CoA by choline acetyltransferase to form acetylcholine
Dietary choline-containing phospholipid that is digested and remodelled, producing circulating choline as one route to the direct choline substrate
Acetyl-group donor combined with choline by choline acetyltransferase to form acetylcholine
Nutritional precursor of coenzyme A, from which cells form the acetyl-CoA required for acetylcholine synthesis

Folate-dependent methyl metabolism helps maintain the brain choline resource available for acetylcholine formation; folate deprivation lowered choline and acetylcholine in studied mouse models, with SAM rescue supporting this upstream resource relationship.

title: Neuronal Membrane DHA Incorporation
mission: Deliver and integrate DHA into neuronal membranes so the brain maintains a flexible, signal-ready lipid foundation.

findings.statement: DHA is a structural polyunsaturated fatty acid of neuronal membranes; that structural role is not a human dosing or ADHD-treatment rule.
LPC-DHA is transported by MFSD2A more efficiently than free or triglyceride-bound DHA; carrier form is a transport property, not a choline-intake or ADHD-dosing rule.
Phospholipid-bound dietary DHA produced greater gray-matter DHA accretion than triglyceride-bound DHA in neonatal piglets; that animal contrast is not a human dosing or ADHD-treatment rule.
Observational multi-nutrient supplementation in ADHD-seeking children is translationally adjacent to attention and emotion scores; it cannot isolate membrane DHA incorporation as the cause.
Human PET estimates of circulating DHA incorporation quantify brain replacement under studied conditions; they do not directly measure oral dose requirements.
Choline tracing supports contribution to the PEMT-derived LPC-DHA route; separate transport experiments establish LPC-DHA as a brain-delivery substrate.

Folate-dependent remethylation and hepatic betaine/BHMT remethylation replenish methionine for SAM-dependent PEMT chemistry, which connects to the independently established methyl-derived LPC-DHA carrier route.

inputs.role: Long-chain omega-3 fatty acid incorporated into neuronal-membrane phospholipids

Choline can contribute methyl groups through the upstream methionine/SAM route to [BRS2 PM7 — PEMT-dependent phosphatidylcholine formation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm3/brs2-fm3-pm7-phosphatidylcholine-formation). Methyl-derived LPC-DHA is a carrier used by MFSD2A for brain DHA delivery.

Folate-derived one-carbon units support [BRS2 PM1 — remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm1-folate-b12-dependent-homocysteine-remethylation), replenishing methionine for SAM-dependent [BRS2 PM7 — PEMT formation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm3/brs2-fm3-pm7-phosphatidylcholine-formation), upstream of DHA-bearing LPC carrier delivery.

Betaine donates a methyl group through hepatic [BRS2 PM2 — BHMT remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation), replenishing methionine/SAM used by [BRS2 PM7 — PEMT formation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm3/brs2-fm3-pm7-phosphatidylcholine-formation) upstream of DHA-bearing LPC carrier delivery.

title: Glutamate Clearance & Recycling
mission: Clear and recycle glutamate efficiently so excitatory load does not overwhelm neural circuits.

findings.statement: Glutamate is the principal excitatory neurotransmitter, and uptake plus recycling are required to terminate synaptic signalling and prevent extracellular accumulation.
Regional glutamate/glutamine spectroscopy associates with attention scores in adults with ADHD and does not measure excitatory amino-acid transporter flux.

title: Excitotoxicity Modulation
mission: Limit excitotoxic pressure when glutamatergic drive is excessive so neural stability is protected over time.

findings.statement: Excessive glutamate-receptor stimulation can produce bioenergetic and excitotoxic stress.
Magnesium sulfate protected against the bioenergetic consequences of chronic glutamate-receptor stimulation in that preclinical model.
Excitation–inhibition network framing is context for this cluster and is not a demonstration of excitotoxic buffering.

title: GABA Synthesis Capacity
mission: Maintain sufficient glutamate decarboxylase capacity, and sufficient PLP cofactor to support it, so GABA can be synthesised from glutamate.

findings.statement: GAD65 and GAD67 differ in their typical PLP-bound states, providing experimental evidence for distinct modes of regulating GABA synthesis. The larger apoenzyme fraction associated with GAD65 suggests potentially recruitable catalytic capacity. However, independent replication of the specific occupancy finding has not yet been established in this assessment, and the physiological importance of this proposed reserve mechanism in the human brain remains uncertain.

In recombinant human pyridoxal kinase (PDXK) assays, zinc was the most effective tested divalent cation under the specified in-vitro metal-to-nucleotide conditions. Activity depends on metal–nucleotide speciation and can be inhibited by pyridoxal, ZnATP and excess free zinc. These experiments do not establish physiological zinc limitation, dietary zinc responsiveness or increased human brain GABA synthesis.

GABA concentration and GABA synthesis rate can move in opposite directions: inhibiting GABA degradation raises GABA concentration while lowering synthesis rate and GAD67 protein, so concentration cannot be used as a measure of synthesis capacity.
Brain GABA concentration in ADHD differs from controls inconsistently by age and region - lower in children, higher in adults - and no study in this body of evidence measured GABA synthesis.

In women with ADHD or borderline personality disorder, lower anterior cingulate GABA concentration is associated with greater aggression, and lower GABA with greater impulsivity, linking the regional GABA pool to affect-regulation outcomes in humans.

Cortical GABA concentration in polysomnography-verified primary insomnia is directionally inconsistent across independent samples - lower, 12% higher, and unchanged - with elevated GABA interpreted as an adaptive allostatic response to chronic hyperarousal.

In the high-dose vitamin B6 trial, self-reported anxiety decreased within the B6 group, but the change-versus-placebo interaction was not significant (p=0.140). The visual surround-suppression interaction was significant (p=0.011). GABA synthesis was not measured.

Genetic abolition of GAD65 in mice alters anxiety-like behaviour in a sex-dependent manner and increases, rather than decreases, preference for social interaction, alongside compensatory changes in cortical interneuron populations.

inputs.role: Substrate for GAD-dependent GABA synthesis
Required cofactor for GAD-dependent conversion of glutamate to GABA
Provides dietary B6 vitamers that pyridoxal kinase converts to PLP, the cofactor required for GAD-dependent GABA synthesis

title: Synaptic Structural Plasticity
mission: Maintain and adapt physical connections between neurons through synapse formation, selective stabilisation, structural remodelling and elimination.

findings.statement: Motor learning in mice produces new dendritic spines and selectively retains a subset as other spines are eliminated.
Activity can induce local BDNF–TrkB signalling and staged actin and postsynaptic scaffold remodelling at individual dendritic spines.
Mouse studies associate sleep with task-related spine formation, REM-dependent selective pruning and reduced size of many ultrastructurally identified synaptic contacts.
In adult mouse neocortex, inhibitory synapse markers and dendritic spines show spatially related structural dynamics influenced by sensory experience.
In the developing mouse visual pathway, microglia engulf presynaptic inputs through activity-sensitive complement signalling.
Uridine and choline contribute to membrane-precursor supply; DHA with UMP increased hippocampal spine density in adult gerbils, while UMP alone did not significantly increase that endpoint.
Two months of voluntary running changed dendritic spine density and selected dendritic structures in adult rat hippocampus and entorhinal cortex.
Spermidine feeding prevented ageing-related enlargement of presynaptic active zones and excess vesicle release in fruit flies without rescuing the age-related loss of synapse number.
Mouse experiments show glucocorticoid-dependent spine formation and elimination, with different effects of physiological and prolonged exposures.
DHA exposure from birth increased pre- and postsynaptic marker abundance in mouse visual cortex; cultured neurons showed additional contact-marker and network responses.
Active-period feeding altered regional spine maintenance in mice previously exposed to high-fat/high-sucrose feeding, alongside memory and activity responses.

inputs.role: Choline supplies the phosphocholine headgroup used to build phosphatidylcholine, a membrane material supporting structural assembly.
Uridine can supply CTP used in CDP-choline and phosphatidylcholine formation, contributing membrane precursors for structural assembly.
DHA supplementation increased hippocampal dendritic spine density in adult gerbils in the studied four-week exposure.

sop.input: Experimental DHA–UMP co-supplementation
Experimental spermidine supplementation in ageing
Active-period feeding under obesogenic exposure (experimental)

title: Folate/B12-Dependent Homocysteine Remethylation
mission: Recycle homocysteine to methionine through folate and B12 so methyl-donor supply and homocysteine control stay supported.

findings.statement: Cobalamin-dependent methionine synthase transfers the methyl group of 5-methyltetrahydrofolate to homocysteine, producing methionine and tetrahydrofolate, and uses methylcobalamin as its cofactor. Betaine-dependent remethylation, methionine adenosyltransferase, transsulfuration and phosphatidylethanolamine methylation are separate reactions.

Flavin adenine dinucleotide derived from riboflavin is a cofactor of methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase and of methionine synthase reductase, not of the methionine synthase catalytic site, which uses methylcobalamin.
A reduction in blood homocysteine after folic acid or vitamin B12 does not measure tissue methionine-synthase flux.
Attached ADHD biomarker and MTHFR-genotype studies do not establish that folate- and B12-dependent methionine synthase activity modulates Focus / Attention Stability.

B-vitamin effects on cognitive decline in mild cognitive impairment, including an interaction with omega-3 status, do not measure methionine synthase flux or establish that this reaction modulates Cognitive Clarity.
A small human tracer study measured increased whole-body remethylation and transmethylation after three weeks of folic acid; concentration changes did not establish those rates.

inputs.role: Methyl-group donor substrate for methionine synthase. The enzyme transfers that methyl group to homocysteine and releases tetrahydrofolate.
Dietary folate, including folic acid reduced by dihydrofolate reductase, is converted through the folate cycle to 5-methyltetrahydrofolate, the methyl donor used by methionine synthase.
Cobalamin cofactor that carries the methyl group from 5-methyltetrahydrofolate to homocysteine during methionine synthase turnover.
Dietary cobalamin is absorbed and processed intracellularly to the methylcobalamin cofactor used by methionine synthase.
Sulfur-amino-acid substrate that methionine synthase remethylates to methionine.

title: Betaine/BHMT Remethylation
mission: Provide a parallel homocysteine clearance route so methionine and SAMe supply remain resilient when folate demand is high.

findings.statement: BHMT transfers a methyl group from betaine to homocysteine, forming methionine and dimethylglycine, without folate or vitamin B12 in that reaction, and uses an active-site zinc ion to activate homocysteine.
Irreversible oxidation of choline to betaine is an upstream supply route for the BHMT substrate and is not itself the BHMT reaction.

Changes in plasma homocysteine after betaine supplementation, choline depletion, or vitamin B12 and fish-oil treatment do not measure tissue BHMT flux and do not establish a clinical benefit of this reaction.
The repository ADHD diet review and choline neurodevelopment review do not directly demonstrate that BHMT-dependent remethylation changes Focus / Attention Stability.
Plasma homocysteine lowering after betaine, and narrative choline reviews, do not directly demonstrate that BHMT-dependent remethylation changes Cognitive Clarity.
Inadequate betaine availability, including from conditional failure of choline provision, can constrain BHMT-dependent homocysteine remethylation capacity.

inputs.role: Methyl-donor substrate for BHMT remethylation of homocysteine to methionine
Dietary precursor that can be oxidised to betaine, the methyl-donor substrate for BHMT
Methyl-acceptor substrate that BHMT converts to methionine
Active-site metal that activates the homocysteine thiol during BHMT catalysis

title: SAMe Synthesis
mission: Maintain methionine adenosyltransferase capacity to convert methionine and ATP into SAMe, sustaining the methyl-donor pool used by downstream methyltransferases.

findings.statement: MAT-dependent SAMe synthesis directly requires methionine and ATP and uses active-site magnesium and potassium ions to support ATP-dependent catalysis.

Measured SAM concentration and the SAM:SAH ratio reflect the balance of synthesis, methyl-group utilisation, SAH formation and clearance and therefore cannot by themselves identify MAT-dependent SAMe synthesis capacity.
The repository-attached mood-disorder evidence does not directly demonstrate an effect of endogenous MAT-dependent SAMe synthesis capacity on Emotional Regulation.
The repository-attached methylation evidence establishes SAMe's donor role but does not directly demonstrate that endogenous MAT-dependent SAMe synthesis capacity modulates Cognitive Clarity.
Folate and betaine remethylation regenerate methionine upstream of MAT-dependent SAMe formation; choline can contribute through betaine.

MAT2B association can preserve MAT2A protein or catalytic stability in purified-human-enzyme and mammalian-cell experiments. This supports a stability contribution to enzyme regulation, not an exclusive explanation of MAT2B action or a demonstrated increase in human SAMe synthesis flux.

inputs.role: Direct amino-acid substrate for MAT-dependent SAMe formation
Direct adenine-nucleotide substrate for MAT-dependent SAMe formation
Active-site metal ion coordinating ATP-derived phosphate groups during MAT catalysis
Active-site metal ion positioning ATP-derived phosphoryl groups during MAT catalysis
Provides methionine through protein digestion and amino-acid absorption; methionine is the direct amino-acid substrate for MAT-dependent SAMe synthesis.

Folate supplies 5-methyltetrahydrofolate to [PM1 — Folate/B12-dependent remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm1-folate-b12-dependent-homocysteine-remethylation), regenerating methionine that PM3 can use to form SAMe.
Betaine donates a methyl group through [PM2 — Betaine/BHMT remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation) to regenerate methionine used by PM3.

Choline can be oxidised to betaine, supplying methyl groups through [PM2 — Betaine/BHMT remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation) for methionine regeneration upstream of PM3.

title: Methionine Cycle Flux
mission: Maintain balanced methionine-cycle flux so methionine availability, SAM-dependent methylation, homocysteine recycling and transsulfuration remain coordinated across changing physiological demand.

findings.statement: Methionine-cycle throughput runs from methionine to SAM, methyl transfer and SAH hydrolysis to homocysteine, after which homocysteine is distributed between remethylation and transsulfuration under the influence of SAM, SAH and methyl-tetrahydrofolate.

Moderate dietary vitamin B6 restriction that lowered plasma pyridoxal 5'-phosphate did not change mean postprandial remethylation, transmethylation or total transsulfuration rates in healthy young adults.
Homocysteine, SAM, SAH and cystathionine concentrations do not measure remethylation, transmethylation or total transsulfuration rates.
Evidence linking homocysteine concentration to cognitive decline or Alzheimer risk does not demonstrate that integrated methionine-cycle rates modulate Cognitive Clarity.
Homocysteine and B-vitamin differences in ADHD cohorts, and dietary-pattern associations, do not demonstrate that integrated methionine-cycle rates determine Focus / Attention Stability.
Folate-dependent remethylation and the mainly hepatic/renal BHMT route return methionine to the integrated cycle; choline can supply betaine.
A small human tracer study measured increased whole-body remethylation and transmethylation after three weeks of folic acid; concentration changes did not establish those rates.

inputs.role: Amino acid that enters the methionine cycle and is regenerated when homocysteine is remethylated
Provides digestible methionine, the amino acid that enters the cycle.
Supplies 5-methyltetrahydrofolate, the methyl donor used when the cycle remethylates homocysteine
Provides the cobalamin cofactor for folate-dependent remethylation of homocysteine inside the cycle
Provides pyridoxal phosphate, the cofactor for the transsulfuration exit that converts homocysteine toward cysteine
Provides the flavin cofactor for the enzyme that makes 5-methyltetrahydrofolate used in remethylation

Betaine donates a methyl group through [PM2 — Betaine/BHMT remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation) to regenerate methionine returned to the integrated methionine cycle.

Choline can be oxidised to betaine, supplying methyl groups through [PM2 — Betaine/BHMT remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation) for methionine regeneration within the integrated methionine cycle.

title: Transsulfuration Pathway
mission: Divert homocysteine toward cysteine so methylation demand is balanced against sulfur amino-acid and redox needs.

findings.statement: Human cystathionine beta-synthase catalyses a pyridoxal 5'-phosphate-dependent condensation of L-serine and L-homocysteine to L-cystathionine, and pyridoxal 5'-phosphate is the active vitamin B6 cofactor recycled from food.
Human cystathionine gamma-lyase requires pyridoxal 5'-phosphate and cleaves L-cystathionine in the transsulfuration step that produces cysteine.

Pyridoxal 5'-phosphate dependence and vitamin B6 salvage do not measure cystathionine beta-synthase or cystathionine gamma-lyase flux and do not prove that vitamin B6 intake controls transsulfuration.
The assessed paediatric ADHD biomarker study does not show that transsulfuration modulates stress reactivity or that it treats stress or ADHD.
Cysteine produced by cystathionine cleavage can supply later glutathione synthesis, but the assessed evidence does not measure recovery capacity.
Moderate vitamin B6 restriction changed cystathionine kinetics without a significant change in total transsulfuration in this small controlled human study.
Primary protein experiments establish SAM-responsive CBS activation; nutritional effects on net transsulfuration depend additionally on substrate allocation.

Combined folate/choline deprivation reduced measured hepatic CBS catalytic activity in rats; donor-resource context can therefore constrain this step under that defined deprivation condition. SAM-responsive CBS regulation is a supported connection, not a measured mediator of the dietary effect.

inputs.role: Active cofactor required by cystathionine beta-synthase and cystathionine gamma-lyase for the homocysteine-to-cysteine conversion.
Food source of the pyridoxal 5'-phosphate cofactor used by cystathionine beta-synthase and cystathionine gamma-lyase, through the vitamin B6 salvage pathway.
Methionine-cycle intermediate that cystathionine beta-synthase condenses with serine to form cystathionine.
Cosubstrate with homocysteine for cystathionine formation by cystathionine beta-synthase.
Pathway intermediate cleaved by cystathionine gamma-lyase in the step that releases cysteine.
Methionine enters the methionine cycle, producing homocysteine that supplies the CBS reaction and carries sulfur into cysteine formation.

title: Glutathione Synthesis
mission: Build glutathione from sulfur amino acids so cellular antioxidant defence stays connected to one-carbon metabolism.

findings.statement: Glutathione synthesis requires ATP-dependent formation of γ-glutamylcysteine from glutamate and cysteine, followed by ATP-dependent addition of glycine, and does not use selenium or riboflavin as synthesis substrates.

Human blood-cell glutathione synthesis can slow when dietary methionine and cysteine are both removed and can rise in older adults after combined cysteine and glycine precursor supplementation, whereas a methionine-adequate cysteine-free diet did not limit erythrocyte synthesis in young men.

Erythrocyte and whole-blood glutathione synthesis rates and concentrations do not measure neuronal glutathione synthesis, do not establish that every person is substrate-limited, and are not ADHD, recovery or stress-resilience outcomes.
The assessed human evidence does not demonstrate that glutathione synthesis capacity changes Recovery Capacity as a functional or clinical outcome.
The assessed human evidence does not demonstrate that glutathione synthesis capacity changes Stress Resilience.

inputs.role: Sulfur-amino-acid substrate joined to glutamate in the first ATP-dependent step of glutathione assembly.
Amino-acid substrate joined to cysteine in the first ATP-dependent step of glutathione assembly.
Amino-acid substrate added to γ-glutamylcysteine in the second ATP-dependent step of glutathione assembly.
Adenine-nucleotide substrate consumed by both glutathione assembly enzymes.
Metal ion bound by human glutathione synthetase, one per subunit, during ATP-dependent glutathione formation.
Supplemental cysteine precursor given with glycine to older adults, in whom erythrocyte glutathione synthesis increased.
Dietary methionine can supply cysteine for glutathione assembly. Methionine is not a substrate of the assembly enzymes.

title: Phosphatidylcholine Formation
mission: Maintain phosphatidylcholine formation through PEMT methylation and the choline-based Kennedy pathway.

findings.statement: Hepatic PEMT converts phosphatidylethanolamine to phosphatidylcholine by three sequential SAMe-dependent methyl transfers. The reaction substrates are phosphatidylethanolamine and SAMe. Magnesium is not an established cofactor of this reaction, and the CDP-choline pathway is a parallel route outside it.

S-adenosylhomocysteine, the product released after each PEMT methyl transfer, can regulate PEMT activity. The attached and retrieved sources do not demonstrate that elevated homocysteine itself inhibits human PEMT.
Neonatal piglet brain DHA accretion and human cerebrospinal-fluid DHA enrichment measure delivery of DHA. They do not measure the rate of hepatic PEMT methylation.

The VITACOG reanalysis shows a B-vitamin by omega-3 interaction on cognitive decline in mild cognitive impairment. It does not measure PEMT activity or phosphatidylcholine formation, so a Cognitive Clarity link is a downstream inference.
Attached diet and choline reviews do not measure PEMT activity or phosphatidylcholine formation. A relationship to Focus / Attention Stability is a downstream inference.
Folate restriction can reduce the contribution of dietary methyl groups to hepatic phosphatidylcholine formation through PEMT in female mice.

Dietary methionine supplies the SAM-dependent PC methylation route. Piglet tracing measures nutritional effects on methyl incorporation into PC, but does not establish a distinct methionine–cysteine pool bottleneck.
Choline and dietary phosphatidylcholine can provide methyl groups used in PEMT-dependent phosphatidylcholine formation.
Uridine can contribute to CTP and CDP-choline supply for the Kennedy route of phosphatidylcholine formation.

inputs.role: Phospholipid substrate that receives three methyl groups during conversion to phosphatidylcholine
Methyl-group donor consumed in each of the three transfers that convert phosphatidylethanolamine to phosphatidylcholine
Dietary choline can provide methyl groups through betaine remethylation and methionine/SAM synthesis for PEMT-dependent formation.
Dietary phosphatidylcholine can provide choline for its methyl-donor provision relationship to PEMT-dependent formation.
Folate availability contributes to the methyl-donor supply used by hepatic PEMT; folate restriction with choline maintained reduced hepatic methyl-derived PC enrichment in female mice.
Betaine can support the methyl-donor supply used by hepatic PEMT; supplementation restored SAM:SAH balance and reported PEMT-mediated PC production in ethanol-fed rats.
Uridine can be converted through nucleotide metabolism into CTP, which helps form the CDP-choline used to build phosphatidylcholine.
CTP reacts with phosphocholine to form CDP-choline in the Kennedy pathway.
Diacylglycerol receives the phosphocholine group from CDP-choline to form phosphatidylcholine.
Choline is phosphorylated to phosphocholine, the choline-containing precursor used by the Kennedy pathway.

title: NF-kB Signalling Regulation
mission: Regulate NF-κB transcriptional tone so pro-inflammatory gene programmes do not fire excessively.

findings.statement: IKK-1 and IKK-2 phosphorylate the NF-κB inhibitor proteins, and IKK-2 is required for NF-κB activation in the cell systems tested. This is an upstream activation step, rather than transcription itself.
Cysteine and glycine supply glutathione used in redox regulation of NF-κB; this establishes upstream supply rather than proven dietary control of transcription.

inputs.role: Canonical NF-κB activation uses IKK (EC 2.7.11.10) to phosphorylate IκB with ATP. Protein-serine/threonine kinases use Mg²⁺–ATP as the phosphoryl donor for that phosphotransfer.

Cysteine supplies a constituent of glutathione. Glutathione participates in the redox regulation of NF-κB kinase activity and DNA binding; this is upstream resource supply, not a direct NF-κB reaction substrate.

Glycine supplies a constituent of glutathione. Glutathione participates in the redox regulation of NF-κB kinase activity and DNA binding; this is upstream resource supply, not a direct NF-κB reaction substrate.

title: Gut-Derived Inflammatory Signalling
mission: Limit gut-derived endotoxin spillover so barrier dysfunction does not drive systemic inflammatory load.

findings.statement: Metabolic endotoxemia is lipopolysaccharide reaching the blood after a change in the gut barrier, with downstream inflammatory signalling through Toll-like receptor 4.

KC1 provides cysteine and glycine for glutathione used in oxidant-sensitive epithelial barrier protection. This resource connection is distinct from the downstream NF-κB response to gut-derived signals.
The defined mouse exposure provides evidence for dietary state regulation, rather than proving fermentable fibre is a necessary substrate for this PM.

inputs.role: Cysteine supplies a constituent of glutathione used in epithelial redox protection. Glutathione prevented oxidant-induced paracellular permeability in a cell model; this supports upstream supply to a barrier-protection route, not a proven dietary reduction in endotoxin spillover.

Glycine supplies a constituent of glutathione used in epithelial redox protection. Glutathione prevented oxidant-induced paracellular permeability in a cell model; this supports upstream supply to a barrier-protection route, not a proven dietary reduction in endotoxin spillover.

title: Nrf2-Mediated Cellular Defence Regulation
mission: Regulate the expression of cellular defence genes in response to oxidative and electrophilic stress.

findings.statement: Keap1 represses Nrf2 until oxidative or electrophilic stress allows defence-gene transcription. Sulforaphane can slow Keap1-directed disposal of Nrf2 in cells. That is regulation, not a dietary requirement.

A myrosinase-completed broccoli sprout homogenate raised phase II enzyme RNA in nasal cells of healthy adults. Extracted sulforaphane capsules did not raise Nrf2 target-gene expression in COPD lung cells.

inputs.role: Modulates KEAP1-mediated control of Nrf2, promoting antioxidant-response gene transcription. Human dietary exposure increased Nrf2-associated phase II enzyme RNA in nasal lavage cells.

sop.input: Myrosinase-completed broccoli sprout homogenate

title: ROS Generation vs Clearance Balance
mission: Balance reactive oxygen species production and clearance so net oxidative pressure stays within tolerable limits.

findings.statement: Mammalian cells clear superoxide and hydrogen peroxide with superoxide dismutase, catalase and glutathione peroxidase. Copper, zinc, manganese, selenium and glutathione belong to those enzymes. That membership is not an intake result.
Glutathione participates in peroxidase clearance of peroxides. That role is biochemical. It is not evidence for eating glutathione.
Dietary selenium restores plasma glutathione peroxidase activity in selenium-deficient adults up to a plateau near 35 micrograms a day. Intake above that plateau did not raise the enzyme further.

Copper repletion raised erythrocyte superoxide dismutase in infants with marginal copper status. Adding copper to the assay tube did not raise the enzyme, so the change tracked copper nutrition rather than copper in the test.

inputs.role: Selenocysteine source for glutathione peroxidase, which clears hydroperoxides
Structural metal in cytosolic copper-zinc superoxide dismutase
Catalytic metal in copper-zinc superoxide dismutase, which converts superoxide to hydrogen peroxide
Catalytic metal in mitochondrial manganese superoxide dismutase
Thiol reductant used by glutathione peroxidase when it clears hydroperoxides

title: Lipid Peroxidation Control
mission: Protect membrane fats from oxidative damage so vulnerable polyunsaturated fatty acids remain intact.

findings.statement: Vitamin E interrupts lipid peroxidation by scavenging peroxyl radicals in the lipid phase. Its vitamin function is protection of polyunsaturated fats in membranes.

A long prevention trial found more prostate cancers with 400 IU of vitamin E a day than with placebo. That result is not a peroxidation measurement, and it is a reason not to treat extra vitamin E as a benefit.

inputs.role: Chain-breaking antioxidant that limits lipid-peroxyl radical propagation in membranes

title: Antioxidant Network Recycling
mission: Regenerate vitamin and thiol antioxidants across networked systems so endogenous defence capacity is sustained.

findings.statement: Vitamin C can reduce the vitamin E radical. That regeneration is a biochemical partnership. It does not set a high-dose intake.

inputs.role: Reduces the vitamin E radical so vitamin E can keep working. This is regeneration, not the chain-breaking job in the membrane.
The lipid-phase antioxidant whose radical is reduced by vitamin C. Chain-breaking in the membrane is a different job.

title: Cytokine Network Modulation
mission: Tune downstream cytokine signalling intensity so inflammatory tone does not remain chronically elevated.

findings.statement: IL-6 and TNF-α are inflammatory messengers used to read this downstream step. They are not the NF-κB transcription step, and an endotoxin challenge did not show that EPA plus DHA significantly changed each of them.

title: Eicosanoid / SPM Balance
mission: Shift lipid mediator balance from pro-inflammatory eicosanoids toward pro-resolving signals that terminate inflammation.

findings.statement: EPA and DHA are the fatty-acid substrates for resolvins and protectins. Those mediators support resolution of inflammation rather than only blocking it.
Five days of 2.4 g a day of n-3 fatty acids raised selected pro-resolving mediators in healthy adults. Not every mediator rose, and aspirin added no further increase.

inputs.role: n-3 fatty-acid substrate for specialised pro-resolving mediator synthesis
n-3 fatty-acid substrate for specialised pro-resolving mediator synthesis

title: Electron Transport Chain Function
mission: Sustain efficient electron transport so mitochondria generate ATP without excessive electron leakage.

findings.statement: Mammalian oxidative phosphorylation oxidises mitochondrial reducing equivalents through five complexes and two mobile carriers, uses iron, copper, haem and flavin mononucleotide (FMN) in the transfers, and couples the proton gradient to ATP synthesis.

Mammalian mitochondria produce superoxide or hydrogen peroxide at defined sites associated with substrate oxidation and the respiratory chain, including complexes I, II and III, rather than by a single uncontrolled leak from the whole chain.

Cybrid cells carrying platelet mitochondria from three boys with ADHD showed lower respiration, lower complex V activity, loss of membrane potential and higher mitochondrial superoxide than control cybrids, without a dietary or attention-outcome test.
The assessed human cell evidence does not show that electron-transport capacity changes Cognitive Energy Stability.

inputs.role: Iron–sulfur clusters and haem irons transfer electrons along the respiratory complexes.
Flavin mononucleotide (FMN) accepts electrons from NADH at the start of complex I.
Riboflavin is the vitamin precursor of flavin mononucleotide (FMN), the flavin that accepts NADH electrons in complex I.
Ubiquinone carries electrons from complexes I and II to complex III.
Complex IV uses two copper centres while it passes electrons to oxygen.

title: NAD⁺ Metabolism
mission: Maintain NAD⁺ availability so redox reactions and mitochondrial signalling stay adequately powered.

findings.statement: Major pathways that maintain the mammalian NAD⁺ pool are de novo synthesis from tryptophan, the Preiss–Handler route from nicotinic acid, and salvage of nicotinamide. Most cells outside the liver depend on salvage. These are not the only precursor entry routes.
NAD⁺ is a substrate of non-redox enzymes, including sirtuins, CD38 and poly(ADP-ribose) polymerases, as well as a hydride acceptor in energy metabolism.
Circadian clock factors control NAMPT-mediated NAD⁺ biosynthesis in mice and cells, so NAD⁺ availability oscillates across the day in those systems.
In adults with mitochondrial myopathy, escalating niacin to 750–1,000 mg/day increased blood NAD⁺ and restored muscle NAD⁺ to the matched-control level, without a cognitive endpoint.
Aerobic and resistance training increased skeletal-muscle NAMPT protein in young and older adults, without a reported change in NAD⁺ concentration.
No assessed study measured NAD⁺ availability against cognitive energy. The ADHD cybrid experiment measured respiration without an NAD⁺ or cognitive-energy endpoint.
No assessed study measured NAD⁺ salvage or NAD⁺ availability against recovery capacity.

inputs.role: Nicotinamide is the salvage substrate that NAMPT recycles toward NAD⁺.

inputs.input: Nicotinic acid (a form of vitamin B3)
inputs.role: Nicotinic acid is the Preiss–Handler substrate that cells convert toward NAD⁺.
The liver can convert tryptophan to nicotinamide, which other cells salvage into NAD⁺.

title: Creatine–Phosphocreatine Energy Buffering
mission: Enable rapid ATP buffering so high-energy-demand tissues can meet sudden metabolic spikes.

findings.statement: Cerebral creatine availability is jointly determined by endogenous synthesis, SLC6A8-mediated transport and cellular compartmentalisation, with more restricted exogenous uptake than in skeletal muscle.
Habitual dietary creatine exposure does not map directly onto posterior-cingulate total creatine concentration in healthy adults.
Exogenous creatine can alter cerebral total creatine or phosphocreatine, with smaller, region- and protocol-dependent responses than in skeletal muscle.
Creatine supplementation does not produce a uniform cognitive benefit in healthy populations; observed effects vary by domain, age, dietary context and study design.
Under acute sleep deprivation, high-dose creatine can modify cerebral high-energy-phosphate measures and partially preserve cognitive performance.
Cooking time, temperature profile and sample location influence creatine retention and creatinine formation in pork matrices.

inputs.role: Creatine accepts and donates phosphate through the reversible creatine-kinase reaction, forming the phosphocreatine reserve used for rapid ATP buffering.
Arginine donates its amidino group to glycine in the first step of endogenous creatine synthesis.
Glycine accepts the amidino group from arginine to form guanidinoacetate, the immediate precursor used in creatine synthesis.
SAM provides the methyl group used to convert guanidinoacetate to creatine through guanidinoacetate methyltransferase.

sop.input: Limit unnecessary cumulative heat exposure when retaining creatine in pork products
Consider creatine monohydrate only in defined low-intake or high-demand contexts

title: ROS Production and Control
mission: Maintain balance between mitochondrial reactive oxygen species production and protective buffering to prevent redox damage.

title: Mitochondrial Protection (Redox Integrity)
mission: Preserve mitochondrial membrane and enzyme integrity so organelle function survives oxidative and metabolic strain.

title: Carnitine-Mediated Fat Transport
mission: Enable long-chain fatty-acid transport into mitochondria so fat-derived ATP production can proceed.

title: Ketone Utilisation Capacity
mission: Enable mitochondrial ketone utilisation so alternative fuel is available when glucose conditions shift.

title: Metabolic Fuel Switching
mission: Shape smooth transitions between glucose, fat, and ketone fuel pathways as physiological demand shifts.

title: Mitochondrial Biogenesis
mission: Enable formation of new mitochondria so long-term energetic capacity can expand and adapt.

title: Gut Barrier / Tight Junction Integrity
mission: Maintain epithelial tight junction integrity and selective permeability at the gut lining.

findings.statement: Intestinal tight-junction structure and regulation determine selective paracellular permeability, while epithelial injury can create a distinct unrestricted permeability pathway.

Butyrate can function as an epithelial metabolic substrate and promote intestinal tight-junction assembly, while fermentable dietary fibre lies upstream as microbial substrate provision for short-chain-fatty-acid production.
Current human evidence provides only indirect observational support for a relationship between intestinal barrier biology and attention-related symptoms.
The bounded evidence assessment does not establish that gut tight-junction integrity modulates Emotional Regulation.
Cellular zinc supports junction-protein maintenance; retinoic acid influences epithelial differentiation and selective permeability.
A placebo-controlled trial in postinfectious IBS with hyperpermeability found improved permeability and symptoms with glutamine.
Specific oligosaccharide and polysaccharide preparations support microbial fermentation upstream of barrier biology.
Ethanol can disrupt epithelial junctions; permeability improved during abstinence in alcohol-dependent patients who began with elevated permeability.
Including fat with the tested vegetable meal increased absorption of provitamin-A carotenoids; its downstream barrier contribution is an upstream supply inference.
One small IBS-D trial reported lower small-bowel permeability during a four-week fermented-milk treatment; a different fermented-milk trial in ileostomy participants found no permeability change.

inputs.role: Microbially produced short-chain fatty acid that serves as a colonocyte energy substrate and directly promotes intestinal tight-junction assembly.
Provides fermentable carbohydrate to gut microbes for short-chain-fatty-acid, including butyrate, production upstream of epithelial barrier effects.
Active vitamin A metabolite involved in epithelial differentiation and permeability regulation; the direction of permeability change varies with experimental context.
Provides dietary retinoids and provitamin A precursors that support formation of retinoic acid for epithelial differentiation and barrier maintenance.
Required cellular mineral for maintenance of occludin and claudin-3 expression and intestinal tight-junction integrity.
Enterocyte metabolic substrate supporting epithelial proliferation, repair, and tight-junction protein maintenance.
The tested FOS/GOS preparation supplies microbial fermentation substrates upstream of epithelial barrier biology.
Pectin provides microbial fermentation substrate that contributes short-chain fatty acids upstream of epithelial barrier biology.
Resistant starch supplies colonic microbes whose fermentation products contribute upstream to epithelial barrier biology.

sop.input: Include dietary fat with provitamin-A vegetables

title: LPS / Endotoxin Containment
mission: Limit host exposure to bacterial endotoxin and related inflammatory microbial products.

findings.statement: Intestinal alkaline phosphatase can reduce responses to selected microbial substrates; its effects on LPS depend on chemical structure.
LPS uptake can occur through lipid-associated transport without requiring increased paracellular leak.
Defined fat-containing meals changed postprandial endotoxin measurements in small human crossover studies.
Oligofructose lowered plasma LPS in a small human trial and mouse experiments; resistant-starch mouse findings do not establish a whole-fibre effect.
One small crossover study found that a defined resveratrol–grape-polyphenol preparation suppressed the meal-associated rise in measured LPS and LBP.
Controlled human emulsifier studies show preparation-specific microbiome or barrier findings rather than a consistent reduction in host LPS exposure from avoiding all emulsifiers.
AOAH-mediated deacylation limited persistence of biologically active LPS and prolonged immune tolerance in mice.
Defined dietary patterns can alter endotoxin readouts, but controlled human studies do not show uniform improvement across patterns or markers.

inputs.role: Oligofructose lowered plasma LPS in adults with overweight/obesity; separate obese-mouse experiments support a GLP-2-sensitive barrier route.
In aged female mice on a high-fat diet, adding 20% type 2 resistant starch lowered serum and faecal LPS and increased colonic mucin.
In twenty healthy adults, serum endotoxin was lower after the tested fish-oil-containing n-3 meal than after the tested coconut-oil-rich meal.
In eight obese men, the same 40 g milk-fat load as an emulsion produced a higher early chylomicron-LPS peak but a lower eight-hour plasma LPS area than a spread.
Zinc participates in intestinal alkaline phosphatase catalysis; purified calf-enzyme experiments show cooperation with magnesium in phosphomonoesterase activity.
Magnesium supports phosphomonoesterase activity of intestinal alkaline phosphatase together with zinc; activity depends on the reaction and substrate.

title: Microbial Barrier–Immune Interface Support
mission: Support intestinal mucus maintenance and mucosal immune regulation through defined microbial activities.

findings.statement: Bifidobacterium longum NCC2705 can prevent impaired colonic mucus growth in a Western-diet mouse model.
Bacteroides fragilis polysaccharide A can protect against experimental intestinal inflammation through an IL-10-dependent immune response.

inputs.role: In Western-diet mice, this inulin preparation prevented increased inner-colonic mucus penetrability; mucus growth was not restored.
Administering this exact strain prevented reduced colonic mucus growth in Western-diet mice.

title: Microbial Substrate-Processing Selection & Adaptation
mission: Adjust community substrate-processing capacity through resource competition and changes in microbial function.

findings.statement: Competition and functional acclimation can change community glycan processing even when several organisms possess relevant utilisation genes.
High-fibre intake can increase metagenomic glycan-processing potential without increased diversity, while fermented-food-associated immune changes do not establish diversity-mediated benefit.
These resistant starch forms provide substrates for specialist microbial degradation and cross-feeding; adding Ruminococcus bromii enhanced RS3 fermentation in one donor’s faecal community in vitro.

inputs.role: Arabinan in the studied pea-fibre preparation supplies a glycan resource whose utilisation depends on microbial utilisation machinery and competition.
The studied citrus pectin supplies glycans for microbial utilisation; community context and expression of utilisation machinery alter processing.
These resistant starch forms provide substrates for specialist microbial degradation and cross-feeding; adding Ruminococcus bromii enhanced RS3 fermentation in one donor’s faecal community in vitro.

title: SCFA Production & Signalling
mission: Maintain short-chain fatty acid production and signalling that supports gut barrier and brain communication.

findings.statement: Resistant starch and pectic substrates can supply microbial SCFA-production capacity; observed responses depend on preparation and community, while the FOS/GOS mixture admission requires review.
Propionate and butyrate affect experimental barrier and mitochondrial endpoints.

inputs.role: Resistant starch reaching the colon supplies fermentable carbohydrate to microbial communities capable of its utilisation, supporting SCFA-production capacity.
The studied FOS/GOS mixture is a candidate microbial carbohydrate substrate; the corrected study does not sufficiently establish the existing PM-specific Capacity admission.
Fermentable polysaccharide supplying microbial SCFA production in human-microbiota culture experiments.
Acetate is a microbial fermentation product involved in metabolic or receptor-mediated signalling; this is product biology, not an oral requirement.
Propionate is a microbial fermentation product involved in metabolic or receptor-mediated signalling; this is product biology, not an oral requirement.
Butyrate is a microbial fermentation product involved in metabolic or receptor-mediated signalling; this is product biology, not an oral requirement.

title: Polyphenol Biotransformation & Mitochondrial-Relevant Metabolite Generation
mission: Enable microbial activation of dietary polyphenols into bioactive metabolites.

findings.statement: Ellagic acid conversion requires microbial activity; particular species perform intermediate steps, and human completion varies.
Administered urolithin A has downstream mitochondrial and experimental cognition findings.

inputs.role: Immediate microbial substrate for the assessed urolithin-generation pathway.
Hydrolysis releases ellagic acid upstream of microbial urolithin formation.

title: Vagal / ENS Signalling Modulation
mission: Maintain gut-to-brain nerve signalling through the vagus nerve and enteric nervous system.

findings.statement: Lactobacillus rhamnosus JB-1 produced vagus-dependent responses in mice; its human trial did not establish stress or cognitive benefit.
Mouse enteroendocrine cells connect to vagal neurons and use glutamate for rapid nutrient signals.

inputs.role: This exact strain elicited vagus-dependent receptor-transcript and behavioural responses in mice.
Luminal glucose acted as a sensory stimulus in the tested mouse neuropod–vagal circuit.
Endogenous transmitter used by neuropod cells for rapid synaptic communication with vagal neurons.

title: Neurotransmitter Precursor Biotransformation & Availability
mission: Maintain gut-side processing that shapes neurotransmitter precursor availability.

findings.statement: A tested apple-pectin exposure altered microbial cross-feeding and tryptophan metabolism.
E. coli tryptophanase contains bound pyridoxal 5′-phosphate in its holo structure.

inputs.role: Immediate substrate used by the microbial tryptophan-processing routes assessed here.
The tested pectin supplies cross-fed carbohydrate that redirects microbial tryptophan processing.
Intracellular catalytic cofactor of the assessed E. coli tryptophanase enzyme.

title: Glucose Appearance Kinetics
mission: Shape the rate of post-meal glucose appearance so metabolic and neuroendocrine systems face manageable, predictable load.

findings.statement: The tested rye bread and high-slowly-digestible-starch cereal product reduced early model-derived meal-glucose appearance in their respective comparisons.
The studied fish-first sequence and whey preload delayed gastric emptying in separate acute comparisons.
Pasta structure survived mastication and simulated digestion; cooling the tested chickpea pasta increased measured resistant starch. Both comparisons also measured lower post-meal glycaemia.

The tested beta-glucan meal shifted exogenous appearance later; a guar/chickpea flatbread blend modestly reduced four-hour exogenous appearance without significantly changing its primary half-absorption-time endpoint.

title: Glycaemic Variability Regulation
mission: Limit glycaemic volatility so post-prandial glucose swings do not create unnecessary metabolic and neuroendocrine stress.

findings.statement: In an uncontrolled cohort of 13 sedentary adults with type 2 diabetes, seven days of aerobic training were associated with lower glucose range and selected excursion measures; high-glucose excursion frequency and duration remained statistically inconclusive.
Fish before rice reduced within-meal glucose variability in the diabetes group.
An observational diabetes study linked glucose fluctuation measures with urinary oxidative-stress markers.
Brief walking interruptions reduced postprandial glucose and insulin exposure versus continuous sitting.

In adults with type 2 diabetes, the tested less-processed whole-grain package reduced daily glucose standard deviation and mean amplitude of glycaemic excursions (MAGE) versus a nutrient-matched finely processed package over two weeks.

In a small prediabetes crossover, the tested early, front-loaded eating schedule reduced mean amplitude of glycaemic excursions (MAGE) over six days versus later calorie distribution; mean glucose and several other variability/range measures were inconclusive.
Two weeks of the tested supervised interval-walking programme reduced mean amplitude of glycaemic excursions (MAGE) versus an inactive control period in a small type 2 diabetes crossover trial.

Four brief vigorous bodyweight bouts daily produced small secondary continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) variability improvements over 48 hours in inactive adults with well-controlled type 2 diabetes; the primary mean-glucose contrast was not significant.

Early eating with front-loaded calories (six-day trial)

title: Metabolic Inflammation & Adipose Stress Signalling

findings.statement: Moderate weight loss improved insulin action before the measured adipose inflammatory markers declined.
EPA-rich supplementation lowered stimulated immune-cell IL-6 production in medical students.

The green-MED trial identifies walnuts as a food candidate, but does not isolate a walnut-specific effect on visceral fat.
Some catechin-enriched tea beverages reduced visceral fat, while a newer catechin-plus-inulin beverage did not.
Marine omega-3 formulations can change adipose inflammatory endpoints, but effects differ across populations and assays.
Adipose expansion is associated with macrophage inflammatory activity, while acute overnutrition can impair metabolism before measured cytokines rise.

Exercise training altered subcutaneous adipose structure without weight loss in adults with obesity.
